rules.title: Replace starter data
rules.summary: Replace neutral starter data with source-backed architecture, release, and project rules before treating Architext as current.
rules.rationale: Fresh installs validate immediately, but starter data is not project-specific documentation.

rules.title: 80% minimum unit-test coverage, mockable integration
rules.summary: Code must reach at least 80% LOC unit-test coverage. Integration/exec code (nettop, lsof, ps, codesign, TCC/sqlite3, terminal screens, network) must be exercised through injectable mocks so tests run in GitHub CI without sudo or external tools; extract pure logic behind seams rather than shelling out in tests.
rules.rationale: GitHub Actions cannot run sudo-gated CLIs or open a real terminal; shelling out in tests is non-hermetic, slow, and fails in the pipeline. Mockable seams keep the codebase both testable and CI-safe.

rules.title: Release ceremony: docs current before the cut, close-out after the tag
rules.summary: Every release runs an ordered ceremony. BEFORE cutting (feature->develop->main->tag), all documentation must be current and validated for the exact scope shipping: Architext Release Truth + index, README, and any release notes describe what the release actually contains, and `architext validate` passes. AFTER the tag, run a post-release close-out stage: flip the shipped Release Truth item(s) to complete/released with the tag as evidence, remove them from any active blocker and open-milestone itemIds, mark the cut milestone complete, and delete temporary artifacts (ABORT/scratch review docs, .bak recovery files, resolved repair-advice entries, throwaway logs). A release is not done until the close-out runs.
rules.rationale: Docs written after a cut describe a moving target and routinely drift; validating scope before the tag keeps the shipped truth honest. Skipping the post-release close-out strands Release Truth mid-flight (stale in-progress/at-risk states, orphaned blocker/milestone itemIds, leftover scratch files) and gives future agents and humans false confidence. Making both stages standing parts of the ceremony prevents the recurring drift where Release Truth reads as unfinished long after a release, or as complete before one is verified.
